data.name: Lioba
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Germanic elements 'lio' (bright, shining) and 'fah' (happy), Lioba means 'Radiant light'. In Christianity, Saint Lioba (652-722 AD) was a Frankish noblewoman who became an abbess and was renowned for her devotion to the poor and her travels to convert the Slavic people.

in_hebrew.name: ליובה
in_hebrew.meaning: ליווה אלוהים את עם ישראל במשך כל הדורות
in_hebrew.long_meaning: ליווה הוא שם שמקורו בגרמנית ומשמעותו 'חביבת אלוהים' או 'אהובה על אלוהים'. השם ליווה מורכב משתי מילים: ‘ליוב’ שפירושו חיבה או אהבה, ו-‘בה’ שפירושו אלוהים. ליווה הוא שם שמשקף את הקשר בין האדם לאלוהים ואת האהבה שבה.

in_greek.name: Λιόβα
in_greek.long_meaning: Το όνομα Λιόβα είναι γερμανικής προέλευσης και σημαίνει 'αγαπημένη του Θεού' ή 'αρεστή στον Θεό'. Στην πνευματική παράδοση, το όνομα Λιόβα συμβολίζει τη σχέση αγάπης και αφοσίωσης προς τον Θεό.

in_latin.name: Lioba
in_latin.long_meaning: Nomen Lioba origine germanicum est et significat 'dilectam Dei' vel 'amatam a Deo'. In traditione christiana, nomen Lioba devotionem et amorem erga Deum repraesentat.

in_english.name: Lioba
in_english.meaning: Lioba means beloved of God or loved by God
in_english.long_meaning: The name Lioba, of Germanic origin, signifies 'beloved of God' or 'loved by God'. Etymologically, it is derived from the German words 'liub' or 'lieb', meaning love or beloved, and a suffix suggesting a relationship with God. Historically, Lioba has been associated with Christian tradition, symbolizing a deep, spiritual bond with the divine. The name conveys a sense of divine favor and affection.

saint_reference.note: Saint Lioba, also Lioba or Leofgyth, was an 8th-century Anglo-Saxon nun, abbess, and missionary to Germany.

historical_references.reference: Lioba, a daughter of the Frankish nobleman Dagobert II, was a Benedictine abbess who is venerated as a saint. She was born in 722 and became a nun at the convent of Chelles under the Abbess Itta. Lioba is best known for her missionary journey to England in 740, where she founded the abbey of Wimborne Minster in Dorset.

Lioba is also remembered for her association with Boniface, the Anglo-Saxon missionary and bishop of the Angles and the Saxons. Boniface had a significant role in Christianizing the Germanic peoples of central Europe during the late 7th and early 8th centuries. Lioba met Boniface while he was in France on missionary work, and they developed a close friendship. Boniface later invited Lioba to England to aid in the evangelization efforts there, where she would go on to establish Wimborne Minster.
